newsitem.title: Australia: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian Broadcasting Corp Midday Update.

text.p: CLAIMS RACIST REMARKS COULD JEOPARDISE GAMES BID
Victorian Premier Jeff Kennett believes Pauline Hanson could cost Victoria support in its bid to host the 2006 Commonwealth Games.
Mr Kennett says the Independent Federal MP needs to temper her views and think very seriously about the damage she is doing to Australia overseas.
And he believes Mrs Hanson has thrown a rock into a calm sea, causing unnecessary disruption.
NO CONFIDENCE MOTION IN QUEENSLAND GOVT
The debate about the future of the Queensland Government has begun in State Parliament with Opposition leader Peter Beattie moving a no confidence motion against it.

Speaking to the motion, Mr Beattie said the shock resignation of Kenneth Carruthers QC starkly demonstrated to all Queenslanders that when the Coalition returned to power, the dark shadow of corruption came with it.

He said the debate is not just about the resignation of Mr Carruthers, who headed an inquiry into pre-election deals between the Coalition and the police union, and Labor and the Sporting Shooters Association.
Mr Beattie says its a debate about whether we want to return to the corruption of the past and about what sort of government Queenslanders want.
NATIONAL BANK CUTS LOAN RATES
The National Australia Bank has announced cuts to some its fixed home loan rates.
The bank is reducing rates on its one to five year fixed loans by as much as one per cent.
The move follows a recent spate of interest rate reductions by other banks and non-bank lenders, in anticipation of an official interest rate cut before Christmas.
AUSTRALIAN-JAPAN TALKS STALLED
The uncertainty following Japan's election has forced the postponement of regular government talks with Australia.
The Australia-Japan Ministerial Committee had been scheduled to meet in Tokyo on November the 11th.
Australia's Foreign Minister, Alexander Downer, said the delay in the formation of the new Japanese Cabinet meant the conference was no longer feasible.
Mr Downer said the talks involving up to half a dozen senior Ministers from both sides would be rescheduled in the near future.
CALL FOR NATIONAL APPROACH ON GAMBLING
Australia's first Professor of Gaming is calling for a national industry strategy.
Jan McMillen, who's to become the Professor of Gaming at Western Sydney University, has expressed concerns at the future of gambling in Australia.
She says it's time to look nationally at how to achieve an economically sustainable gambling industry, which also deals with its social impact.
She says every Australian spends at least 500-dollars a year on gambling, more than they spend on alcohol.
CUP FAVOURITE NOT FOR SALE
Melbourne Cup favourite Oscar Schindler is not for sale.
It now appears the reported asking price of four million dollars wouldn't be enough to buy the Irish Champion.
Owner Oliver Lehane faced the racing media this morning confident that his horse would go into Tuesday's race in top form.
He told the crowd if they don't back Oscar Schindler to win don't bet on anything else to beat him.
EVIDENCE IN BLACKHAWK INQUIRY CONTINUES
The Blackhawk inquiry has heard of further staff shortages in the Army's Fifth Aviation Regiment
The military board inquiry into the mid air collision which killed 18 soldiers in June, also heard that a soldier whose job it was to provide photos, wasn't trained to take them.
The Inquiry has heard on the night the accident the targets on the courter-terrorism exercise were difficult identify.
A white board map depicting them was inaccurate and there were no photos available of Fire Support Base Barbara, where the targets were located.
Corporal Peter Hill told the inquiry he was the only member of the intelligence cell which he joined ten months ago.
He said for exercise he never recieved written orders from the SAS.
